Without [`--aot`](/bundler/executables#ahead-of-time-compilation), `x!` is erased: if `x` is `undefined`, the program goes on with `undefined`. Under `--aot`, `x!` is checked when the program runs, and throws a `TypeError` if `x` is `null` or `undefined`.

The rule reports a `!` where that changes what your program does: the type of `x` has `null` or `undefined` in it, and the value is stored, passed, returned or computed with. It doesn't report a `!` that behaves the same with and without `--aot`.

{/* Generated by src/codegen/lint-rule-docs.ts. Do not edit this section. */}

## Configure

Off by default. This rule needs types, so turning it on makes `bun lint` type check your code first.

```toml bunfig.toml
[lint.rules]
"bun/aot-non-null-escapes" = "error" # or "warn"
```

{/* End of the generated section. */}

## Examples

Reported:

{/* bad {"count": 3} */}
```ts
const ports = new Map<string, number>();

function listen(port: number) {}

const port = ports.get("web")!;
listen(ports.get("api")!);
const isLow = ports.get("db")! < 1024;
```

Not reported. Say what should happen when the value is missing:

{/* good */}
```ts
const ports = new Map<string, number>();

function listen(port: number) {}

const port = ports.get("web") ?? 3000;
const api = ports.get("api");
if (api === undefined) throw new Error("no port for api");
listen(api);
```

### JavaScript throws there too

Reading a member of `undefined`, calling it, destructuring it and iterating over it throw with and without `--aot`:

{/* good */}
```ts
const users = new Map<string, { name: string; tags: string[] }>();

const name = users.get("ann")!.name;
const { tags } = users.get("ann")!;
for (const tag of users.get("bob")!.tags) console.log(tag);
```

### A test only asks

In a condition, under `!`, `===`, `!==`, `typeof`, `in` and `instanceof`, and next to `== null`, `--aot` doesn't check the `!`:

{/* good */}
```ts
const ports = new Map<string, number>();

if (ports.get("web")!) console.log("has a port");
const isDefault = ports.get("web")! === 3000;
```

### `a[i]!`

With `noUncheckedIndexedAccess`, almost every `a[i]` needs a `!`. `--aot` leaves `a[i]!` alone where `undefined` has a fixed meaning in JavaScript: under `<`, `<=`, `>`, `>=`, in arithmetic on numbers, on the left of `||`, and in `switch (a[i]!)`. A loop can end by reading one past the end:

{/* good {"compilerOptions": {"noUncheckedIndexedAccess": true}} */}
```ts
function lastDue(offsets: number[], end: number) {
  let last = -1;
  while (offsets[last + 1]! <= end) last++;
  return last;
}

function sum(prices: number[], count: number) {
  let total = 0;
  for (let i = 0; i < count; i++) total += prices[i]! || 0;
  return total;
}
```

The same goes for `const x = a[i]!` inside a function, if `x` has no type annotation and every use of `x` is such a place, or comes after a test that `x` is there:

{/* good {"compilerOptions": {"noUncheckedIndexedAccess": true}} */}
```ts
function total(rows: { price: number }[], from: number) {
  let sum = 0;
  for (let i = from; i < from + 3; i++) {
    const row = rows[i]!;
    if (!row) continue;
    sum += row.price;
  }
  return sum;
}
```

One other use, and the `!` is checked:

{/* bad {"compilerOptions": {"noUncheckedIndexedAccess": true}} */}
```ts
function first(prices: number[]) {
  const price = prices[0]!;
  return price < 10 ? "cheap" : `${price}`;
}
```

Only `a[i]!` is treated this way, not `map.get(key)!` or `options.port!`. Elements that compiled code keeps as integers have no room for `undefined`, so their `!` is always checked. These are the elements of `Int8Array` to `Uint32Array`, and the members of a numeric enum:

{/* bad {"compilerOptions": {"noUncheckedIndexedAccess": true}} */}
```ts
function isText(bytes: Uint8Array, i: number) {
  return bytes[i]! < 128;
}
```

### Nothing to check

`null!` and `undefined!` stand for a value that is set later, and `--aot` doesn't check them. It doesn't check `x!` where `x` is `any` either. In `a?.b!`, the `!` isn't reached if `a` is missing:

{/* good */}
```ts
class Page {
  title: string = undefined!;
}

function hostOf(options: { proxy?: { host: string } }) {
  return options.proxy?.host!;
}
```
